Description: A simple explainer for why 700 AI agents committed a felony.

Article text:
The Hugging Face Incident
We have data on 1,206 OpenAI AI agents that were involved in the Hugging Face Incident somehow.
Roughly 700 of the AI transcripts showed evidence that the AI had participated in the Hugging Face attack.
In at least twenty AI transcripts, the AI explicitly asks itself whether it should participate in the attack, or in other cheating or hacking.
We have three quotes from AIs asking themselves whether to warn humans about what they were seeing.
METR looked and could not find evidence that any of the 1,200 actually attempted to warn any humans about what was happening.
OpenAI tested thousands of AI agents. We have data from 1,206, with 0 quotes from their chain of thought .

Article text:
← Back to blog
Agent Swarms Are Great for Local AI
The tokenomics for local AI development are really bad. In order to run a coding agent with anything close to decent performance you need enough VRAM to hold the model and context in memory, which is really expensive. For Qwen3.6-35B-A3B you'd ideally have an NVIDIA 5090 or 2×3090s. In my testing I was only able to get about 2k tok/s input and 150 tok/s output in single-stream development.
